insight.title: How a Simple Metal Box Built the Modern World
insight.subtitle: Why standardization is the hidden force behind global trade.

sections.text: Before standard shipping containers, moving goods was a slow and expensive mess. Workers carried sacks, barrels, and crates by hand onto ships. It took weeks to load a single vessel. This inefficiency made imported products incredibly expensive for normal people. Everything changed when a simple, uniform metal box was finally invented.

In the 1950s, a businessman named Malcolm McLean promoted a standard size for these boxes. Now, every container fits perfectly on a truck, a train, or a massive ship. Because every port uses the same locking system, machines do the heavy lifting. This allows for incredibly fast and reliable global loading.

Standardization collapsed the cost of shipping across the oceans. Today, it is cheaper to send a sweater across the globe than to mail it to a neighbor. This efficiency created the modern world. It allows businesses to build things anywhere, giving us easy access to affordable food, clothes, and technology.

news.title: What's Coming in the M5 MacBook Air
news.description: Along with the low-cost MacBook, Apple could introduce a refreshed version of the MacBook Air next week. Most of the focus will be on the new machine, but the MacBook Air is expected to get some useful internal updates. M5 Chip The next-generation MacBook Air will adopt the M5 chip, which Apple already introduced in the iPad Pro and MacBook Pro models that came out last year.

news.title: Researchers reveal why SuperAgers retain youthful brain cell signatures into their 80s
news.description: Researchers used single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling to map human hippocampal neurogenesis across adulthood, aging, and Alzheimer’s disease. They found that chromatin accessibility changes, more than gene expression alone, distinguish healthy aging, preclinical pathology, Alzheimer’s disease, and cognitive resilience in SuperAgers.

news.title: RNA, Reimagined: The Nobel Discovery That Still Shapes Science Today
news.description: There have been many important discoveries along the path to what we know today about RNA, or ribonucleic acid—a molecule found in every living cell that helps carry and interpret genetic instructions.
